title: Jacob I loved, Esau I hated
note: Readers in the line of Augustine, Reformed readers above all, take the passage of God's choice of particular persons to salvation, made before they were born and resting on his mercy alone, not on anything foreseen in them.

Many Greek Fathers, with Arminian and Wesleyan readers, read it of God's freedom to choose peoples and callings in his plan, Israel and the nations, and hold that his choice of persons takes account of the faith he foresees. Catholic theologians have held views across this range, all teaching that grace goes before every good act and that the will freely consents to it. These readings differ within churches as well as between them.
common: All read the passage as teaching that God's call rests on his mercy, and not on anything people have done.
